templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Switch off the lights when not in use to save electricity.'
Assumption I: Electricity is produced at some cost.
Assumption II: People sometimes leave lights on unnecessarily.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The advice implies people leave lights on unnecessarily (II) — target behaviour. That electricity needs to be saved (I) is also implicit. Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'To maintain good health, avoid junk food.'
Assumption I: Junk food is harmful to health.
Assumption II: People eat junk food regularly.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Junk food being harmful (I) is the foundation of the advice — implicit. Assumption II (people regularly eat junk food) is not assumed — the advice is general. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Kindly carry your identity card at all times during the examination.'
Assumption I: Students may forget to carry their identity cards.
Assumption II: Identity cards help verify the student's identity.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The reminder assumes students may forget (I) — reason for the reminder. Identity cards verifying identity (II) is the purpose — also implicit. Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Trees should be planted along roadsides.'
Assumption I: Trees provide shade and improve air quality.
Assumption II: Roadsides currently have no trees.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Trees providing benefits (I) is the reason for planting — implicit. Assumption II (no current trees) is not assumed — planting can happen even if some trees exist. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'An advertisement: Visit our new store for the best deals in town.'
Assumption I: People are looking for good deals.
Assumption II: The store has better deals than other stores.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: People looking for deals (I) is implicit — target audience motivation. The store having the best deals (II) is the claim being made, not an assumption. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Smoking is injurious to health — statutory warning on cigarette packs.'
Assumption I: People smoke cigarettes.
Assumption II: Warning messages discourage smoking.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: A warning on cigarette packs assumes people smoke (I). It also assumes warnings are effective (II) — otherwise, why put them? Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The school has arranged extra classes for students who failed the test.'
Assumption I: Extra classes will help improve students' performance.
Assumption II: The students who failed want to improve.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Extra classes helping (I) is the rationale — implicit. Assumption II (students want to improve) cannot be assumed from the school's arrangement. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'All passengers must fasten their seat belts during takeoff and landing.'
Assumption I: Seat belts improve passenger safety.
Assumption II: Some passengers may not fasten seat belts on their own.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Seat belts improving safety (I) is the reason for the rule — implicit. The rule implies some passengers may not comply on their own (II) — also implicit. Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Start your day with a glass of warm lemon water for better digestion.'
Assumption I: Warm lemon water aids digestion.
Assumption II: Everyone has digestive problems.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Lemon water aiding digestion (I) is the basis of the advice — implicit. Assumption II (everyone has digestive problems) is too strong — the advice can be for general wellness. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The government has launched a scheme to provide free mid-day meals in schools.'
Assumption I: Many school children are malnourished.
Assumption II: Free meals will attract more children to attend school.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Both are implicit. The scheme assumes some children are malnourished (I) — motivation for free meals. It also assumes meals improve attendance (II) — an expected outcome that justifies the scheme.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Read the instructions carefully before operating the machine.'
Assumption I: Operating without instructions may cause damage or injury.
Assumption II: The machine is difficult to operate.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The instruction assumes risk without reading instructions (I) — the reason for the warning. That the machine is difficult (II) is not necessarily assumed — even simple machines need instructions. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Citizens should vote in every election to strengthen democracy.'
Assumption I: Voting strengthens democracy.
Assumption II: Many citizens do not vote.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Voting strengthening democracy (I) is the stated reason — implicit. Assumption II (many don't vote) explains why the appeal is made — also implicit. Both are implicit.
